svg.title: TCP/IP networking fundamentals visual map — full packet journey from browser to server with layer-by-layer breakdown and attacker angles
svg.desc: A full visual diagram showing how data flows from your laptop to google.com through the four TCP/IP layers: Application, Transport, Internet, and Network Access. Each layer shows protocols, key concepts, and how attackers exploit it. The bottom half shows the packet journey: DNS lookup, TCP handshake, IP routing, and ARP resolution.
svg.text: TCP/IP — how the internet actually works
Every layer, every attack, the full packet journey

g.text: What apps use to talk · HTTP · HTTPS · DNS · SSH · FTP · SMTP
TCP = reliable + ordered · UDP = fast, no guarantee · Ports = apartment numbers
UDP — fire and forget, no confirm
MAC addresses · Ethernet · Wi-Fi · ARP (IP → MAC translation)
ARP: "Who has 192.168.1.1? Tell me your MAC"

svg.text: The full journey — what happens when you type google.com
Connection established — data can now flow
ARP — how your laptop finds the router on local network

g.text: ⚠ ARP Poisoning attack — attacker sends fake "I am the router" to all devices → intercepts all traffic (Man-in-the-Middle)
ROS2 connection: DDS uses UDP (Layer 3) · ROS topics = app layer · Multi-machine nodes use IP routing
